newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: War-ravaged Tajikistan's Treasury up and running.
newsitem.headline: War-ravaged Tajikistan's Treasury up and running.

text.p: Tajikistan has set up a Treasury to bring order to its war-ravaged economy as it develops market reforms, a senior official said on Friday.

"In line with a government order, the central office of the Treasury has already started working, and we hope to set up a network of branches in all 73 districts of the country by the end of 1997," Treasury director Akram Suleimanov told Reuters.
Suleimanov said the creation of the national Treasury, helped by the International Monatary Fund (IMF), was "an important step on the road of market reforms."
"We are advancing a bit faster than expected initially," Nirmala Dhume, IMF adviser to the Treasury, told Reuters.
Suleimanov said the Treasury and its branches nationwide will enable the government to monitor all budget revenues and spending and tighten financial discipline.
"This is very important for the republic, which has lived through a civil war and faces serious economic difficulties," he said.
Economic reform in the Central Asian republic has been set back by a bitter four-year civil war in which tens of thousands of people have been killed and many more displaced.
But under IMF guidance, Tajikistan managed to slash inflation to 60 percent last year from 2,223 percent in 1995.
A first IMF loan to Tajikistan worth $22 million agreed to in May last year has helped stabilise the Tajik rouble currency.
